question: Can one LLM be trained to do both text embedding and text generation at best-in-class quality, and what does that buy for RAG?
hypothesis: Generative and embedding training can be unified via instructions with no performance loss on either, since both need deep language understanding.
contributions: GRIT: joint generative and representational instruction tuning in one model
GritLM 7B (MTEB SOTA among open models) and GritLM 8x7B (best open generative model tried)
Ablations: bidirectional attention + mean pooling, in-batch negatives from same dataset, mixed sample/token loss, BF16
RAG caching (query, doc, query-doc, doc-query) giving >60% speedup for long documents
Reranking with same model; memory-saving embedding training technique

method.summary: Finetune all parameters of Mistral 7B / Mixtral 8x7B on embedding data (contrastive loss with in-batch negatives, bidirectional attention, mean pooling) and generative data (next-token loss, causal attention) jointly, distinguishing the modes by prompt format (<|embed|> vs <|assistant|>). Adds RAG caching schemes exploiting the single model.
method.task: unified text embedding and instruction-following generation; RAG

datasets.name: E5S (E5 + S2ORC)
datasets.source: Wang et al. E5 data, adds 80,000 S2ORC

datasets.name: Tulu 2
datasets.preprocessing: filtered custom prompts about model origin

datasets.name: MEDI2
datasets.source: new version of MEDI with better negatives (authors)

datasets.name: MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, TyDi QA, HumanEvalSynthesize, AlpacaEval 1.0

models.name: GritLM 7B
models.architecture: decoder-only, sliding window attention; bidirectional for embedding, causal for generation
models.context: arbitrary via sliding window; trained 2048 tokens

training.objective: L = lambda_Rep*L_Rep + lambda_Gen*L_Gen; InfoNCE with in-batch negatives (Eq 1) plus next-token loss on response tokens (Eq 2), mix of sample and token level (32->8)
training.precision: BF16 mixed precision; pooling and similarity in FP32
training.hardware: 7B: 8 nodes x 8 A100 80GB, 48 h; 8x7B: 32 nodes x 8 H100 80GB, 80 h
training.compute: 3,072 GPU hours (7B); 20,480 GPU hours (8x7B); Gen-only 72 and Emb-only 1760 H100 hours; ~100,000 GPU hours total with ablations

other.lambda_values: not stated; initial loss ratio L_Rep/L_Gen 4.1 for final E5S run (Table 6k)
other.memory: FSDP, gradient checkpointing, FlashAttention-2, triplet splitting, GradCache/distributed in-batch negatives (App H)

inference.temperature: 0.2 for HumanEvalSynthesize pass@1 (20 samples); greedy elsewhere
inference.max_tokens: 6144 for AlpacaEval; 16 generated tokens in RAG latency tests
inference.samples: HumanEvalSynthesize 20 samples; latency std over 100 runs
inference.prompting: Tulu-style chat format; MTEB instructions per dataset (App P); 0-shot unless stated
inference.retrieval: NQ index of 2,681,468 docs; GritLM embeddings; top-1 context inferred from examples; no embedding instruction in RAG

parameters.rerank: top 10, permutation generation prompt from Sun et al.

metrics.name: MTEB average
metrics.definition: mean over 56 datasets of task metrics (Acc, V-measure, AP, MAP, nDCG@10, Spearman)

metrics.name: generative average
metrics.definition: mean of MMLU EM, GSM8K EM, BBH EM, TyDi QA F1, HumanEval pass@1, AlpacaEval win %

metrics.name: match
metrics.definition: any gold answer appears anywhere in the generation

metrics.name: latency
metrics.definition: seconds per example on CPU / H100

baselines: Llama 2 / Tulu 2 / Mixtral Instruct / Zephyr / GPT-4
eval.protocol: single runs, no seeds or significance tests reported; ablations use varied training lengths

evidence.quote: Our learning rate is 2e-5, we use 3% of steps for linear warm-up of the learning rate and decay it linearly to 0 over training.

results.claim: GritLM 7B reaches 66.8 MTEB average (56 datasets), state of the art among open models, equal to the embedding-only variant.
results.setup: Mistral 7B finetuned with GRIT on E5S + Tulu 2; 56 MTEB datasets; batch 2048 emb / 256 gen

results.claim: Llama 2 70B used for embedding without finetuning scores only 35.6 on MTEB.
results.setup: weighted-mean pooling, no embedding finetuning

results.claim: GritLM 7B generative average is 55.5, on par with the generative-only variant (55.2).
results.setup: MMLU, GSM8K, BBH, TyDi QA, HumanEval, AlpacaEval; greedy

results.claim: GritLM 8x7B has the best generative average among open models tried (65.7) and 65.7 MTEB.
results.setup: embedding batch size cut to 256 due to compute

results.claim: Embedding-only and generative-only variants perform near random on the other task (MMLU 23.5 vs 25.0 random; gen-only MTEB 41.2).
results.setup: Gen.-only 7B evaluated on MTEB with weighted-mean pooling
results.quote: benchmarking the embedding performance of the generative-only model only leads to a score of 41.2

results.claim: Reranking the top 10 with GritLM's generative mode lifts the mean retrieval nDCG from 57.4 to 57.9.
results.setup: 15 retrieval datasets, permutation generation prompt of Sun et al., top 10
results.note: Improves 15 of 16 datasets per conclusion; Quora drops 89.47 to 88.67 (table lists 15 datasets).
results.table: Table 3, row Average, columns No Rerank / Rerank top 10

results.claim: One-shot examples in embedding prompts generally hurt performance.
results.setup: 12 MTEB datasets, E5S and MEDI2 trained models, 0 vs 1 FS
results.quote: We find that providing few-shot examples overall worsens performance.

results.claim: KTO alignment after GRIT raises AlpacaEval win rate by more than 10 points while MTEB drops slightly (66.8 to 66.7; 65.7 to 65.2).
results.setup: binarized UltraFeedback, no embedding training during KTO
results.quote: Notably, AlpacaEval jumps by >10 points for both models.

results.claim: Bidirectional attention with mean pooling over the embedding gives the best embedding score in the unified model (64.0 vs 62.8 causal weighted-mean).
results.setup: MEDI embedding data, Mistral 7B, ablation
results.table: Table 6a, Unified, row Bidirectional/Causal/Mean, column Emb

results.claim: Larger embedding batch (4096 vs 256) gives +1.0 embedding average at stable generative score.
results.setup: ablation with MEDI2
results.quote: This leads to a 1.0 gain on the embedding average while generative performance remains stable.

results.claim: E5 embedding dataset beats MEDI and MEDI2 (66.0 vs 64.0, 64.7).
results.setup: unified, bidirectional, mean pooling

results.claim: Mixing sample- and token-level generative loss (32->8) is best: Emb 66.7, Gen 55.4; Mix (4->64) cuts AlpacaEval by about 7 points.
results.setup: E5S unified; Mix(4->64) on MEDI2 gives AlpacaEval 67.6 vs 74.7

results.claim: Down-projecting embedding from 4096 to 1024 costs about 1% embedding performance.
results.setup: linear head only on embedding
results.table: Table 6e, rows No head / -> 1024, column Emb

results.claim: BF16 mixed precision matches FP32 training (66.5 vs 66.3 Emb); pooling and similarity must be FP32.
results.setup: E5S, bs 2048

results.claim: Query Caching is 54% (CPU) and 33% (GPU) faster for long queries; Doc Caching is 63% (CPU) and 31% (GPU) faster for 4000-token documents.
results.setup: GritLM 7B, NQ, 16 generated tokens, Xeon 8481C CPU, one H100, 4000-token query or document
results.quote: For Doc Caching it is 63% and 31% (Sample A).

results.claim: Doc Caching gives the best NQ match score of all variants (33.38 vs RAG 30.50) but needs about 30TB storage of key-value states vs 43GB.
results.setup: 2,681,468-doc BEIR NQ index; KV states in bf16
results.table: Table 7, row Doc Caching, column Match

results.claim: Query Caching drops match to 25.46 vs RAG 30.50 (No RAG 21.00); Query-Doc / Doc-Query caching land near No RAG (21.63, 18.39).
results.setup: same as above; bidirectional embed attention mismatches causal KV states
results.table: Table 7, rows Query Caching, Query-Doc Caching, Doc-Query Caching

results.claim: A separate BGE embedder with GritLM 7B as generator gives only about 10 match on NQ versus 30.5 with GritLM's own retrieval.
results.setup: Query then document prompt, same index

results.claim: Doc Caching holds or improves on RAG for TriviaQA (57.93 vs 52.12) and MMLU (53.46 vs 51.10).
results.setup: same setup as Table 7

results.claim: Training cost: GritLM 7B used 3,072 A100 GPU hours; 8x7B used 20,480 H100 GPU hours.
results.setup: 8 nodes x 8 A100 80GB for 48 h; 1253 steps

limits: Embedding temperature tau and loss weights not given numerically; seeds and variance not reported.
GritLM 7B is far costlier than small embedders (BGE Large 0.34B) and 4096-dim vectors need 4x storage vs 1024.
Doc Caching needs about 30TB of KV states for 2.68M documents; Query-Doc caching hurts quality due to attention mismatch; fix (RAG finetuning) left to future work.
Embedding quality on sequences longer than 512 tokens untested for lack of benchmarks.
Few-shot embedding does not help; 8x7B embedding slightly lower due to smaller batch.
Tulu 2 may be tuned to the generative eval sets; RAG tested on small NQ index with a single match metric inspected on 20 samples.
Ablations are partly sequential, with settings changing between tables, so numbers are not comparable across tables.
Models of 2024; later embedding models likely surpass MTEB score.
